title: Mirik lake and tea slopes weekend
start: NJP railway station or Bagdogra airport
end: NJP railway station or Bagdogra airport

cost_split.item: Reserved car NJP–Mirik both ways and local sightseeing
Hotel or GTA cottage, 2 nights with breakfast

meta_description: Mirik in 2 nights from ₹8,500: Tingling and Sourenee tea views, Sumendu Lake, Bokar Monastery and Rameetay Dara, with an easy family pace and real costs.
summary: An easy family weekend in Mirik. Drive up via Dudhia with stops at the Tingling and Sourenee tea viewpoints, walk Sumendu Lake at dawn, sit in on morning prayers at Bokar Monastery and spend an afternoon among tea and orange slopes. From about ₹8,500 per person.
intro: Mirik is the gentlest hill town in the Darjeeling hills, two hours from Siliguri and built around a lake. This weekend uses a reserved car for the drives, so children and older family members are comfortable, and a single base for two nights so nobody has to pack twice.

We time the sights to avoid the crowds: the lake at dawn, the monastery at prayer time, the tea viewpoints in morning light on the way up. Afternoons are free for boating, a walk on the estate roads or simply a long tea by the water.
highlights: Tea and orange slopes around town

days.title: Up via Dudhia, Tingling and Sourenee
days.drive: ≈ 52 km · 2–3 h by reserved car with stops
days.text: Meet your car at NJP or Bagdogra and drive through Siliguri and Matigara to Dudhia, where the road crosses the Balason. Climb through forest and tea to the Tingling viewpoint, with its bowl of gardens and views west to Nepal, and stop again at Sourenee. Reach Mirik for a late lunch and check in. In the late afternoon, walk to the footbridge and watch the light go off the lake.

days.title: Lake at dawn, Bokar and Rameetay Dara
days.drive: Local car for the monastery hill, ≈ 10 min
days.text: Walk the 3.5 km road round Sumendu Lake at 6 am, before the day-trip cars arrive. After breakfast, drive or walk up to Bokar Monastery, founded by Bokar Rinpoche in 1984, and sit quietly during prayers. Walk on to Rameetay Dara for the view over the lake and valley. In the afternoon, take a rowing boat, or walk out of town along an estate road into the tea and, in winter, the orange orchards.

days.title: Back down to NJP
days.text: Have breakfast and a last walk by the lake. Leave Mirik by 10 or 11 am to reach NJP or Bagdogra by early afternoon, with a stop at Dudhia if you want to see the Balason river. Allow extra time on Sundays and holidays, when traffic into Siliguri is heavy.

includes: Jeeps and reserved cars as listed
Homestays and mid-range rooms on twin sharing
Dinner and breakfast at homestays; breakfast at hotels
excludes: Flights and trains to NJP or Bagdogra
save_money: Go up by reserved car for the viewpoints and come down by shared jeep at ₹150–200 a seat.
Skip the 'five-point' sightseeing packages; the lake, monastery and viewpoint are all walkable.
Stay midweek; Mirik hotels charge more on Friday and Saturday nights.
good_to_know: Mirik fills with day-trippers on weekends and holidays from late morning.
Bokar Monastery is free; dress modestly and ask before photographing inside.
Book well ahead for Puja, Diwali and Christmas.

faqs.a: Yes. ₹8,500 is per person on twin sharing for Indian nationals, from NJP or Bagdogra and back, as an indicative 2025–26 figure. Solo travellers pay more for rooms and cars; groups of four sharing a car pay less. We round to the nearest ₹500.

faqs.q: Can we start from Bagdogra airport instead of NJP?
faqs.a: Yes. Bagdogra is about 30 minutes from Siliguri and a little further from NJP. Shared autos and taxis link the airport to the Siliguri jeep stands. With a reserved car, the fare from Bagdogra is about the same as from NJP.

faqs.q: Can we change the number of nights?
faqs.a: Yes. Add a night where you want more time, usually in the village stops, or drop one on a tight schedule. Keep at least two nights in any place where you want a clear dawn view, since weather can spoil one morning.

faqs.q: Is Mirik good for a family weekend?
faqs.a: Yes. The drives are short, the lake walk is level, boats and ponies keep children busy and food is easy. We keep to one hotel for both nights. Bring warm layers for the evenings and keep children close on the lakeside road.

faqs.q: Where do you suggest staying in Mirik?
faqs.a: The GTA's Swiss Cottages above the lake suit families who want space and quiet. Krishnanagar, across the lake, has many budget and mid-range hotels from about ₹1,200 a double. Choose a lake-view room if your budget allows.

faqs.q: Can we add Darjeeling to this trip?
faqs.a: Yes. Instead of returning to NJP on day 3, drive about 2 hours over the ridge via Sukhia Pokhari to Darjeeling, and spend two nights there. A car from Mirik to Darjeeling costs about ₹2,500–3,200.

faqs.q: What is the best season for this weekend?
faqs.a: October to December for clear weather and oranges from November; March to May for spring and tea. Avoid the heavy rain of July and August. Winter nights are cold, so ask for a heater.

faqs.q: Do we need a guide in Mirik?
faqs.a: No. Mirik is small and easy to explore on your own. Drivers are happy to suggest stops on the way up. A local guide is useful only if you want to walk deeper into the tea estates.

faqs.q: Can older travellers manage this trip?
faqs.a: Yes. Most of it is by car, and the lake walk is level. The climb to Bokar Monastery is steep on foot, but a car can go up. Take it slowly on the stairs at Rameetay Dara.
